messages:
incidents-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty fired: billing-usage-token-skew-service (PD-6321) — threshold breach on token_count_delta. Root TS: 2245678901. Link: https://pagerduty.example/PD-6321

pagerduty: Incident created PD-6321 (billing-usage-token-skew-service) — triggered by metric: token_count_delta > 2,000,000 for 5m. Escalation policy: billing-ops -> eng-sre.

alex: acked. I'm on it, taking first-touch.

maria: thanks alex. quick context: last deploy yesterday touched the checkpoint committer for the usage consumer. we've had intermittent reorders before but never this magnitude.

sam: seeing same alert on dashboards — consumer lag on topic "usage-events-v2" partition 7. consumer offset commit falling behind by ~14m events.

praveen: pulling logs now. tailing consumer-7 logs:
```
2026-03-14T02:45:12Z consumer-7 ERROR commit failed: TimeoutError write lock
2026-03-14T02:46:03Z consumer-7 WARN processing backlog: 13.8m events
2026-03-14T02:47:01Z consumer-7 INFO checkpoint persisted 0 events (skipped due to partition-reorg)
```

maria: ugh. that checkpoint message matches the spike in token delta — if commits skipped, token counts for some customers won't reflect recent usage.

alex: can we confirm which downstream aggregation job uses those commits for invoice windows? need to know customer impact.

billing-ops-bot: Affected invoice window: 2026-03-13T22:00:00Z - 2026-03-14T02:00:00Z. Potentially delayed invoice calculations: ~18 accounts (priority: high x3).

sam: running quick query to get token delta by customer for the last checkpoint window:
```
SELECT customer_id, SUM(tokens) as delta
FROM usage_events_staging
WHERE event_time >= '2026-03-13T22:00:00Z' AND event_time < '2026-03-14T02:00:00Z'
GROUP BY customer_id
ORDER BY delta DESC
LIMIT 25;
```

sam: preliminary shows two customers with unexplained +1.2M and +890k token deltas respectively compared to committed ledger.

praveen: hypothesis: consumer-7 rebalanced and replayed events, causing duplicate counting in staging before dedupe. Also commits failing means ledger didn't advance.

maria: action items: 1) stop invoice job kickoff for the affected window (prevent invoice generation with bad counts). 2) increase consumer replica count for partition 7 and rotate leader. 3) run dedupe backfill on staging for the window. 4) notify CS for potential customer inquiries.

alex: I'm pausing invoice job now (manual toggle). `POST /admin/invoices/pause?window=2026-03-13T22` returned 200.

pagerduty: PD-6321 acknowledged by alex. Next escalation to eng-sre in 15 minutes if not resolved.

praveen: scaling consumer group: `kubectl -n billing scale deployment usage-consumer-7 --replicas=4` — executed. watching pod restarts.

incidents-bot: Autoscaler note: pod usage-consumer-7-2 restarted (OOMKill) after restart attempt; new pod scheduled.

sam: after scaling, partition leader moved to node3, offset commit resumed but commit lag still fluctuating.

maria: starting dedupe backfill job in read-only mode to compute corrected deltas (no write). command: `./bin/dedupe_backfill --topic usage-events-v2 --start '2026-03-13T22' --end '2026-03-14T02' --dry-run`

alex: good. while backfill runs, can we compute estimated revenue risk? asking finance.

taylor: (from finance) quick calc: the two top customers represent ~42% of invoice $ risk for that window — if invoices go out wrong we risk netting ~USD 120k of mis-billed usage. We recommend invoice hold until counts reconciled.

maria: agreed — invoices on hold. CS notified to prep outreach for top 10 customers.

praveen: dedupe dry-run found ~1.15M duplicate tokens for customer A and ~880k for customer B. root cause: consumer replayed messages during partition rebalance while commit timeout persisted.

sam: we have a small patch to commit logic that changes from at-least-once to at-most-once commit ordering for checkpoint writer; needs a canary rollout. we can patch consumer image and rollout to partition 7 first.

alex: what's ETA to safe rollback/patch?

maria: patch build is ready — `gcr.io/redwood/usage-consumer:hotfix-2026-03-14-1`. We should canary to partition 7 then expand if stable for 10m.

jordan: night oncall here, taking handoff at 03:10Z. I'll monitor the canary and stay on until resolved. please post status updates in thread before handoff.

alex: handoff noted. pushing hotfix to consumer-7 canary now: `kubectl set image deployment/usage-consumer-7 usage-consumer=gcr.io/redwood/usage-consumer:hotfix-2026-03-14-1` — started.

incidents-bot: Canary deployment started for usage-consumer-7. Observability: commit_latency metric instrumented.

praveen: after canary start, commit_latency dropped from 12s -> 450ms on canary pod; no duplicate deltas observed in dry-run compare for canary shard.

sam: dedupe backfill dry-run reports indicate corrected totals match expected ledger for canary range. Looks good.

maria: OK let's promote patch to all usage-consumer replicas after a 10m stable window.

alex: promoting to full fleet now. rolling update in progress. `kubectl rollout status deployment/usage-consumer` — 5/5 updated.

billing-ops-bot: Invoice window still on hold. Hold reason: token_discrepancy_remediation_in_progress.

taylor: finance approves release of invoices once we verify final ledger totals and run reconciliation job. please flag when reconciliation completes.

praveen: running reconciler: `python tools/reconcile_ledger.py --window '2026-03-13T22' --apply --verify` — will post output.

sam: reconciler output:
```
2026-03-14T03:05:12Z reconciliation START window=2026-03-13T22
2026-03-14T03:07:48Z reconciliation OK mismatches corrected: 18 accounts normalized
2026-03-14T03:08:03Z reconciliation PASS checksums match ledger
```

maria: checksum match confirmed.

alex: unpausing invoice job. `POST /admin/invoices/unpause?window=2026-03-13T22` -> 200. kicking off invoice generation.

incidents-bot: PD-6321: Incident status -> resolved by alex at 2245679167. Root cause: checkpoint commit timeouts during partition rebalance led to duplicate staging counts; fixed by hotfix changing commit ordering and scaling replicas.

pagerduty: PD-6321 resolved. Resolution note: hotfix rollout + reconciliation.

jordan: taking follow-up: creating post-incident checklist and a quick blameless writeup. I'll link the doc in this thread.

maria: immediate follow-ups: 1) revert temporary scaling if not needed 2) test commit timeout handling in integration 3) add metric for commit_fail_rate alerting 4) run a small chaos test for partition rebalances in staging.

alex: thanks all. CS: update top customers that invoices are complete and correct, apologize for delay.

taylor: confirmed invoices sent and finance validated totals. no customer disputes filed in first 2 hours. closing loop. :white_check_mark:

jordan: will draft a short postmortem and link here by EOD. handing off to on-call docs.

incidents-bot: incident PD-6321 closed.
